concepts.angle: Runners are told to lift less. The opposite is true if you sequence it.
concepts.hook: lift heavy, run easy, never on the same legs

slides.text: most people run their legs into the ground, then wonder why nothing grows.
two lifting days. three easy runs. the hard days stay hard.
your easy run should feel insultingly slow. that is the entire point.
one long run a week. everything else is maintenance for that one.
eight weeks of this beats eight months of doing both badly.

concepts.angle: The unglamorous inputs separate people after year five.
concepts.hook: the athletes still improving after five years do less

slides.text: they protect sleep like a training session, because it is one.
they take the deload week even when they feel fine. especially then.

slides.text: they never train through a sharp pain. dull, maybe. sharp, never.
adding is easy. subtracting is what moves you forward.
